brief: Design an offline welcome and wayfinding kit for the first Repair Night at a neighborhood hall. Doors at 17:30, last intake 19:15. Registration is by the west entrance; electronics is in the back room, sewing by the stage, refreshments in the courtyard. The accessible entrance is on Pine Street. Volunteers need something usable at the door and attendees need to find their way. Choose the medium, assets, and organization yourself.

A public library is running a seed swap on April 12 from 10 to 2. First-time gardeners are welcome, even with nothing to trade. Packs need a plant name and harvest year, and the quiet table is available for questions. Design an offline communications kit the library could actually print or show at the event. Decide what to make and give the event its own visual identity.

Build a small original audio drama package for two performers, about a station platform that appears on an obsolete timetable. The performance is for a community radio slot of about three minutes and must work without a narrator or licensed music. Deliver something the performers and producer can rehearse and stage; the story, production choices and file organization are yours.

Make a small original literary zine called Borrowed Window for an independent book fair. Its subject is two neighbors who see the same street differently. Give it a satisfying ending and a form that makes sense for a pocket-size edition. The stall volunteers should be able to use what you deliver. Choose voice, structure, assets, and format.

A local museum needs a defensible, self-contained exhibit research package on a fictional historical tramway. The ledger gives year, annual passenger journeys (thousands), total fare revenue (thousands of crowns), and annual service km (thousands): 1891 84 42 24; 1892 94 47 25; 1893 97 48 25; 1894 88 45 23; 1895 108 53 27; 1896 115 58 28. A six-week bridge closure was recorded in 1894; the ledger has no daily entries. Investigate the change in ridership and service. Decide what the curator needs to verify the arithmetic and what visitors should see. Use only these fictional records.

Build a compact retrospective analyst package on a fictional orchard packing cooperative. Each row gives season, crates sold, revenue and operating cost in crowns: 1924 900 7200 6000; 1925 1050 7770 6550; 1926 1200 8160 7120; 1927 980 7644 7130; 1928 1350 9990 8430; 1929 1430 10296 9180. New sorting equipment arrived in late 1927; the accounts do not split varieties or capital expenditure. Explain to the cooperative board what changed in margins and what the records can support. Leave an auditable deliverable. Work only from these fictional figures.

Build a small offline utility for the library coordinator to check a volunteer rota. It should identify overlapping assignments for a volunteer, accept back-to-back shifts, and describe invalid time entries usefully. Choose a practical interface and file format. Include what a coordinator needs to try it and what a maintainer needs to verify it. It must work without installing packages or contacting a server.

Create a small offline packing-list tool for a community theater moving props. Staff need to record boxes and props, tell which items have not been assigned, and print a readable inventory by box. Choose the interface, data format, and delivery structure. Include a way to try it and check its behavior. It must run without installing dependencies or using the network.
